tagline: Reclaimed water. Renewable power. A forest, simulated.
description: NetLave explores treated-wastewater forestry in Egypt through a simulation-driven digital twin prototype, connecting reclaimed water, renewable power and explainable irrigation control.
claimLimit: Built on synthetic site assumptions, not field measurements. The prototype is not synchronized with or calibrated against a real installation and does not establish real-world savings, electrical autonomy or regulatory compliance.
safetyBoundary: Synthetic water-quality flags never authorize real-world irrigation. HOLD or UNKNOWN blocks irrigation; manual commands cannot bypass safety gates. A real Egyptian TSE deployment requires current reuse approvals, treatment-grade checks, species authorization, worker protection and monitoring.
modelLimit: Salinity transport, pathogens, tree growth and carbon sequestration are not modelled. The 3D view is a schematic, not to scale; tree color is a moisture-stress proxy, not measured health.
authority: One deterministic Python engine owns physical state and advances in 60-second steps. The dashboard displays snapshots; the landing and product websites explain the model without running physics or showing live field telemetry.
controllerStatus: Smart hysteresis remains the default. Resource-aware scheduling is experimental and opt-in: held-out validation did not establish service non-inferiority at every endpoint, so no automatic promotion or savings claim follows.
evidence: In the published synthetic baseline (seed 7, 14 days), smart hysteresis did not save water and used more pump energy than the ET-sized fixed timer. This historical startup-inclusive diagnostic is not the later warm-up/held-out scheduler validation or a field result.

scenarios.label: Baseline
scenarios.summary: With all zones just below the moisture trigger, A and C start irrigating; B waits on the shared 140 m³/h gravity manifold.

scenarios.label: Clogged filter
scenarios.summary: Solids loading ×8 reduces Zone B's available head while A runs. At clog index 0.60, a five-minute flush uses 1.5 m³ and 0.10 kWh; B can irrigate after head recovers.

scenarios.label: Low solar (sandstorm)
scenarios.summary: Cloud factor 0.25 and initial battery charge 24%: the uphill pump runs about 13 minutes, then stops at the 20% reserve with zero delivered flow.

scenarios.label: TSE interruption
scenarios.summary: No inflow from 06:30 to 12:30 on day one. Micro-hydro falls to zero and the reservoir draws down; a low-storage denial occurs only if its gate is reached.
